title: Analysis server: origin check, upload size cap, extension check, bounded jobs
description:
`analysis/apricity_analyze/server.py` binds to 127.0.0.1 (250) but trusts any page in the browser:
- `/api/upload` (191-201) is a multipart POST, a CORS simple request, so any website the user visits can call it. It overwrites `samples/uploads/<name>` with no existence check and starts ML analysis threads.
- The whole file is read into memory (`await file.read()`, 198) with no size limit.
- No Host-header validation, so DNS rebinding could read `/files/...` and `PUT /api/score` (160-167), which writes arbitrary content to any `.apr`/`.yaml` under examples/ or scores/.
- `/api/analyze` (204-210) does not check the extension and spawns an unbounded daemon thread per call; `JOBS` (172) is never cleaned up.
- `_summary` (63-99) indexes `m["tonal"]["key"]` and `m["rhythm"]["bpm"]` directly, so one malformed or older manifest turns `/api/samples` into a 500 for the whole library. The broad `except Exception` at 143 and 187 reduces failures to `str(e)` with no logging.

Done when: TrustedHost and an Origin check (or a per-session token) guard every mutating route; uploads are size-capped and streamed to disk; analysis runs through a bounded queue with job expiry; a malformed manifest is skipped with a logged warning; tests cover a foreign-origin upload being refused and a bad manifest being skipped.
